response: Combining antiretroviral agents in a single dosage form may have a minimal impact on the quality of life of HIV/AIDS patients. Although the cost-effectiveness of a single-pill strategy was within the acceptable willingness-to-pay threshold, the difference in quality-adjusted life years (QALY) was found to be minimal. Further research is recommended to explore the long-term impact of this strategy on the quality of life of HIV/AIDS patients.
